newsitem.title: USA: Coastal Physician says it may lack cash.
newsitem.headline: Coastal Physician says it may lack cash.

text.p: Coastal Physician Group Inc said on Wednesday that it may lack the cash to meet short-term needs and it may not be able to repay its debt due July 1997.
The company, which expects a fourth quarter loss of $55 million to $65 million, said it is in talks with a lending group to provide additional funding, but reaching a deal may be difficult.

Coastal Physician said the operating losses incurred by the company, divestitures of non-core businesses and principal repayments to its lenders have reduced cash flow available to meet cash operating requirements.
Fourth quarter operating revenue is expected to be $125 million, compared with $181 million in the year ago period.

The company's available credit was reduced to $10 million from $40 million under a previous agreement, Coastal Physician said. The company used the entire amount available during January to meet its most pressing operating requirements, it said.
Coastal Physician said it is obligated to pay all of its outstanding indebtedness of $78 million, as of January 31, 1997, by July.

The company may not be able to meet this obligation unless its existing lenders amend the current repayment terms, alternate financing is arranged, an equity infusion is obtained, or the company sells some assets, Coastal Physician said.
The company's board recently approved the active marketing of its physician contract services unit to generate funds to cut its bank indebtedness, Coastal Physician said.
Coastal Physician said it has retained Smith Barney to market the physician contract unit and to explore alternative sources of financing.
The company has entered talks with another lender regarding its financing needs, it said.
No guarantees could be made about new financing or the sale of the physician contract business, Coastal Physician said.
